objectives.description: Calculate annual compound growth and compare it with simple interest.
Explain why reinvested interest increases the amount earned each year.

sources.reference: Annual compound-interest identity: A = P × (1 + r/100)^t; simple A = P × (1 + r/100 × t).
sources.assumptions: Constant annual rate, annual compounding, no deposits, fees, tax or inflation.

flashcards.prompt: What balance is compound interest calculated on?
flashcards.answer: The current balance, including interest already earned.

quizzes.prompt: At 10% annually, what is $1,000 worth after two years of compounding?

options.feedback: This uses simple interest. Year two earns $110 on $1,100.
This is the balance after only one year.

writtenTests.promptTemplate: Start with ${principal} at {ratePercent}% annually. Calculate the balance after {years} years of annual compounding and show your method.

constraints: Rate is constant and annual compounding is explicit.

rubric.criterion: Correctly substitutes principal, rate and duration.
Applies compounding for the full duration.
